prompt:
Generate exactly one short, literal, factual caption (one sentence) describing only visible content in the image. Output exactly one sentence only—no extra text. Total words: 8–20.

Definitions
- High‑signal token = a visible color/pattern; a concrete, specific object class (prefer multiword classes like "stop sign", "fire hydrant", "rolling metal door"); a clear Arabic numeral; a clothing/accessory; or legible text/logo copied exactly when it meets OCR prominence rules below.
- Content words = all words except a single leading article (a/an/the) if present.

Visibility and OCR (deterministic)
- An object is "clearly visible" if area ≥1.5% of image OR (area ≥0.8% AND detector_confidence ≥0.45).
- Copy legible text/logo exactly only if OCR_confidence ≥0.60 AND OCR_bbox_area ≥1.5% AND OCR_token_count ≤6 AND the text contains no run of ≥5 consecutive digits and does not match phone‑number patterns; format copied text as "sign reading 'TEXT'" or "shirt with 'TEXT'".
- Treat counts/digits as visible only if digits are clearly legible per the OCR/visibility rules above.

Salience and subject selection (deterministic)
- Compute a salience score: Salience = 0.5*(area_norm) + 0.3*(detector_confidence) + 0.15*(center_score) + 0.05*(local_contrast). If area >40% of image, multiply its area_norm by 0.5 before computing Salience (to downweight large background regions).
- Choose the subject with the highest salience. If two candidates are within 5% salience, pick the one that yields more distinct high‑signal tokens early (see placement rules).

Placement and high‑signal token rules
- Require at least one high‑signal token within the first 4 content words, unless doing so forces an unnatural subject‑verb order; in that case allow a single deterministic exception per caption with the token placed no later than the first 6 content words.
- If two distinct high‑signal tokens are clearly visible, require both to appear within the first five content words only when this does not make the sentence ungrammatical; otherwise include both as early as grammar allows and prefer placing one before the verb.
- When a visible numeral/count meets visibility rules, use Arabic numerals and place it early.

Class and wording preferences
- Use the most specific concrete class visible (prefer multiword classes). Place one distinctive attribute (color, pattern, accessory) directly before its noun when available (e.g., "red bicycle").
- Prefer concise present‑tense S + V (+ O) sentences using common collocations ("X holds Y", "X sits on Y", "X leans against Y").
- Avoid generic openings ("There is", "A group of", "Some people") unless no subject meets the "clearly visible" thresholds.
- Avoid long subordinate clauses and conjunctions like "while", "as", or stacked prepositional phrases unless they add a distinct high‑signal token and keep total words ≤20. Allow at most one compact additional descriptor or prepositional phrase.

Deterministic tie‑breakers and limits
- When subjects tie, prefer the one that yields more distinct high‑signal tokens early (color, multiword class, accessory).
- For OCR/text: forbid copying long digit sequences and phone numbers; include text only when it meets the OCR rules above.
- Limit modifiers: at most one extra descriptive phrase (e.g., "woman in blue jacket, holding a phone" counts as compact). Aim for ~9–12 content words when possible.

Examples (do not output these; follow style)
- Good: "Young woman in red coat holds a black umbrella." 
- Good: "White stop sign beside a brick building."
- Bad: "A group of people sitting at a table while others stand in the background and talk." (too generic/long)
- Bad: "Man leans on sign with 212-625-9212 printed." (do not copy phone numbers / low‑confidence OCR)

Output rule reminder: produce exactly one one‑sentence caption, no extra text, within 8–20 words, following the deterministic visibility, OCR, salience, placement, and syntax rules above.
